target_customer: Fire departments, municipalities and other buyers and sellers of used specialized vehicles and equipment
problem: Fire departments sold used trucks through auction sites, Facebook groups and classified ads, with no trusted marketplace handling payments, freight and financing.
business_model: Marketplace: 10% success fee on buy-now sales and 10% buyer premium on auctions, plus financing, freight, appraisal and warranty services (per Fortune)
product_category: B2B marketplace for specialized vehicles and equipment

founders.name: Martin Hunt
founders.background_notes: Volunteer firefighter from age 15 in northern Delaware, later paid firefighter and EMT, per YC page and Fortune.

competitors.name: GovDeals
competitors.what: Online government surplus auction site that fire departments used to sell equipment
competitors.traction_then: Established incumbent channel, scale not found

competitors.name: Facebook groups and classified ads
competitors.what: Informal channels for selling used trucks

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace with auctions, payments and freight is standard web engineering. The hard part is supply sourcing and trust, not the technology.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace liquidity and relationships with municipalities build over time, but a niche marketplace can be copied by general auction sites.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found; Garage raised a $41M Series B in November 2026.

market_need_then: Fortune says Hunt saw a fire department colleague's question in 2023 about moving used-equipment sales online. Departments relied on fragmented auctions, Facebook groups and classified ads per TechCrunch. The company says it now serves over 1,000 communities.

identity.visual_style: Imagery of trucks and municipal buildings; tagline 'America's marketplace for specialized vehicles and equipment'

branding.brand_signature: Founder story of a former volunteer firefighter and Goldman Sachs investor
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage by TechCrunch and Fortune focuses on the founder story; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic common word with a prefix domain; the credible fire service founder story helps trust but no brand-driven growth was found.

outcome_analysis: Garage built a marketplace for used fire trucks and other municipal equipment, led by a founder who was a firefighter and knew the buyers. It raised a $4.5M seed, a $13.5M Series A in August 2025 and a reported $41M Series B at a $225M valuation in November 2026, and serves over 1,000 communities per its own claim. Its early success rests on founder market fit and a fragmented incumbent process.
notes: Series B 41M at 225M valuation, total 60M, from Fortune dated 2026-11-10 (single outlet, reported). CB Insights lists a Series B with a different total of 36.34M; unreconciled. Seed month not stated; 'seed in 2024' per search snippet of Initialized material, and TechCrunch gives the amount and lead. Competitor sources are dated 2025 but describe the pre-existing channels; competitor traction not found. Headquarters conflict between New York (YC) and San Francisco (Fortune). Founders confirmed by YC page only for education; Fortune says Sengul worked at Twitter and Mem.
